chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man acknowledges a debt to an inheritor.' He said, 'It is permissible if he is wealthy (has the means to pay).'
ai.seo_question: Is a debt acknowledgment to an inheritor valid if the debtor is poor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a dying man's acknowledgment of debt to an heir is legally binding provided the debtor is 'maliyy' (wealthy or solvent), a condition that safeguards the estate's value against frivolous claims. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on verifying the financial capacity of the debtor to ensure the inheritance distribution is just and practically enforceable. The requirement of 'maliyy' distinguishes this from cases where a debtor might falsely acknowledge debt to reduce the estate if they lack the means to pay.
